summary: Ashutosh Mishra works in Indology and other fields. He earned his Master of Library and Information Science from the Central University of Gujarat (2020–2022) and held library posts at IRMA (2022–2024), Bennett University (2024), and Parul University (2024–2026).

Ashutosh Mukherjee was educated at South Suburban School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta (BA ~1880–1883). He served at the Calcutta High Court (1904), as University of Calcutta's Tagore Professor of Law (1906–1914), and as Asiatic Society President (~1907–1915).

Ashutosh Pareek is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Rajasthan Sanskrit University (2012) and UGC NET (2005). He served as a professor at Government College, Ajmer (2008) and as visiting faculty at Hindu University of America.

Asim Kumar Chatterjee works in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta under D. Mukherjee (~1963–1967), later serving there as a senior research fellow (attested 1970) and as lecturer in English at Jangipur College.

Indologist and linguist Asko Parpola completed his Ph.D. at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto (1959–1968), also studying under R. Panneerselvam and P. R. Subramanian. He held positions at the Academy of Finland and was professor at Helsinki (~1982–2020).
Assa Doron, an Indology scholar, completed his PhD at La Trobe University (2000–2005). He was appointed Professor at the Australian National University in 2007.

Archaeologist Astley John Hilary Goodwin was educated at St. John's College, Johannesburg (1912–1918), Selwyn College (1919–1922), and SOAS University of London (1922). He joined the University of Cape Town in 1923.

Astrid Zotter, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, received her PhD from the University of Leipzig. Her career includes posts at the University of Lausanne (attested 2012), the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018), and Heidelberg University (attested 2023).
Athanaric Huard is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Georges-Jean Pinault. Huard held a post as Assistent at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).
Linguist and Indologist Athanasius Pryor Treweek studied at the University of Sydney (~1929–1934). He subsequently served at the University of Sydney as Professor of Greek beginning in 1938.

Historian and religious studies scholar Atsuhiko Yoshida studied at Seikei, Tokyo, and Strasbourg universities, the EPHE, and under Georges Dumézil. He held posts at CNRS (~1960–1966), Geneva, UCLA, Seikei University (professor, 1970), and Gakushuin University (professor, 2006).

Atsuki Nakagami specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Nakagami served as a visiting researcher at the University of Hamburg (attested 2022) and held affiliations attested in 2026 with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, Rissho University, and the University of Tokyo.
Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and served as a professor at Toyo University (~2005).

Atsushi Kanazawa, an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher, was educated at the University of Tokyo. Kanazawa taught at the Meteorological College (attested 1989–1990) and served as assistant professor (~1993–2004) and faculty (~2004) at Komazawa University.
Atsushi Kiyozawa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Delhi and served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).

Atsushi Uno, working in Indology and philosophy, studied at Kyoto and Banaras Hindu universities under T. R. V. Murti, Raghunath Giri, and others. He held academic posts at Shuchiin, Kyoto, Tokai, Hiroshima (professor, 1974–1986), and Kindai (professor, ~1986–1993).

Atsuuji Ashikaga worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, studying at Doshisha and Kyoto under Ryosaburo Sakaki. He held multiple academic posts at Kyoto University (1930–1962), Tokai University (~1967–1975), and the Society for Near Eastern Studies in Japan.
Atsuyoshi Keika is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who served at Otani University as a lecturer (attested 1990) and later as a professor (attested 2014).

Atul Chandra Chatterjee, active in Indology and history/archaeology, studied at Calcutta and Presidency under Charles Henry Tawney, and at King's College, Cambridge. He served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1897 to 1931.

Audrey Truschke is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She held research fellowships at the University of Cambridge (~2012–2013) and Stanford University (~2013–2016), an affiliation at UC Berkeley (attested 2014), and faculty appointments at Rutgers University from ~2016.
